reader_question: How many of every 100 workers belong to a union?
grade_line: Documented: a Bureau of Labor Statistics survey, as the atlas records it on October 15, 2026
title: One in ten U.S. wage and salary workers belonged to a union in 2025.
measure_line: Union members as a share of employed wage and salary workers, 2025 annual average, drawn as people out of 100, United States
notes: The share stood at 20.1 percent in 1983. In 2025 it was 5.9 percent in the private sector and 32.9 percent in the public sector, with 14.7 million members in all.
The Bureau says the 2025 average, which leaves out October, is not strictly comparable with other years’ averages.
chart_notes: Each square stands for one worker in 100. The 10 squares filled in the text’s ink are union members, and the 90 open squares are the rest. The drawing beside the words Worker bargaining power is the atlas’s symbol for that variable.
alt: A grid of 100 squares, one for each worker in 100. The first row of 10 is filled for union members in 2025, and the other 90 are open.

table.caption: Union members as a share of employed wage and salary workers; the 2025 figures average 11 months, since the October 2025 survey was not collected

source_line: Source: U.S. Bureau of Labor Statistics, Union Members, 2025 (February 18, 2026), employed wage and salary workers, 2025, United States, as recorded in Oath & Action’s systems atlas, Who Do They Answer To?
